2021_224_000_tsd_pep_study_report_110920.paragraph: A draft Pupil Enrollment Projection Study Report for 2022-2026, prepared by Plante Moran Cresa, LLC of Southfield, Michigan and presented to the Troy School District on November 9, 2021, applies the Cohort Survival Method to district FTE pupil counts and Oakland County live-birth statistics. Based on the 2021 fall FTE count, K-12 general education enrollment is projected to decline from 12,196 in 2021-2022 to 11,408 by 2026-2027, with all-pupil district totals moving from 12,771 to 11,985 across the same span. The 40-page report also compiles U.S. Census demographic profiles for the district, Oakland County, and Michigan.

## Overview
Pupil Enrollment Projection Study Report 2022-2026, presented to the Troy School District on November 9, 2021 by Plante Moran Cresa, LLC (pmcresa.com), Southfield, Michigan. Every page is stamped D R A F T; the document runs 40 pages. Contact for questions: Paul R. Wills, AIA, LEED AP, Partner, 248 223-3316. Four sections: School District (boundary map and general characteristics), Demographic Information, Projection Methodology, and District-Wide Pupil Enrollment Projections using FTE Data.

## Section 1 - School District
Boundary map for the district in Oakland County, grade range KG-12, county FIPS code 26125. Facilities identified include elementary schools Costello, Leonard, Wattles, Wass, Bemis, Hill, Barnard, Schroeder, Martell, Troy Union, Morse and Hamilton; middle schools Larson, Smith, Boulan Park and Baker; high schools Troy Athens, Troy High, International Academy East, and Niles Community High School & Continuing Education Center; plus the Service Center, Transportation Department, Board of Education, and Buildings & Grounds / Purchasing Department.

Enrolled school age children PK-12 in the district total 12,430, of whom 89.54% attend public K-12 schools and 10.46% private. Median year moved in is 2009 for the district.

## Section 2 - Demographic Information
District trends compare 2010, 2020 and 2025 (CBSA Detroit-Warren-Dearborn). Total population moves 64,680 / 67,596 / 68,456. Age 0-5 population moves 4,185 / 4,019 / 3,810 (variance -209, -5.2%); age 6-11 moves 5,414 / 5,354 / 5,203; age 12-17 moves 6,202 / 6,082 / 5,886. Enrolled public school PK-12 moves 11,488 / 10,646 / 10,526. Households earning $200K+ move 3,093 / 6,025 / 7,212 (variance 1,187, 19.7%). Oakland County population moves 1,202,362 / 1,258,791 / 1,274,812. Oakland County live births by year of residence, sourced from the Michigan Resident Birth Files (MDHHS Division for Vital Records & Health Statistics), fall from 17,008 at the start of the 1990-2020 series to 13,078 for 2020, which is flagged as an estimate.

## Sections 3 and 4 - Methodology and Projections
Projections use the standard Cohort Survival Method, with historical FTE data from Michigan Department of Education Form DS-4061 and blended counts calculated as 90% of the fall count plus 10% of the spring count. Two projection sets are presented, one based on the 2021 fall FTE count and one on the 2021 blended FTE count; 2021 data is headcount, to be updated to FTE when available.

CONTENTS. Section 1 covers the School District (boundary map, general characteristics). Section 2 covers Demographic Information (school district demographic report, county demographic report, and county live birth statistics 1990-2020). Section 3 covers the Pupil Enrollment Projection Methodology. Section 4 covers District-Wide Pupil Enrollment Projections using FTE Data (historical pupil count summary, fall projections, blended projections).

SECTION 3 - METHODOLOGY. Plante Moran Cresa uses the standard Cohort Survival Method, comparing pupils in a grade last year against the next advanced grade this year; the worked example states that 100 first grade pupils last year and 112 second grade pupils this year produce a survival ratio of 112%. Projections based on Full Time Equivalent or head counts include only mainstreamed pre-kindergarten through grade 12 pupils, with special education pupils counted as general education by percentage of time in general education classrooms; adult participants and self-contained special education pupils are excluded from history and projections. Historical FTE data comes from Michigan Department of Education Form DS-4061. County live births are used to project the K% Birth proportion, and the current year's births are estimated because the Department of Health cannot compile all county birth statistics until at the earliest the fourth quarter of the following year. Historical columns cover the past 6 years plus the current year; survival ratios for the past seven years are extended out five to ten years. The projections do not account for the closing or opening of a private or chartered school, consolidation, annexation, or re-zoning. The methodology flow chart runs from live births, historical enrollment, community trends and community demographics through a first pass projection, baseline establishment, comparison to trend, a second pass projection, and review, verify and confirm.
